title: Convert numbers, mask bits, and pack bytes
brief: Write base conversion, bit masks and shifts, two's complement, and little- and big-endian packing, then use them to read and write a bytearray memory.
hints: To convert to base b, repeat: take `n % b` as the next digit (lowest first), then `n //= b`. Look digits up in the string `"0123456789abcdef"`. Reverse at the end, and handle 0 on its own.

To read a string in base b, start with `total = 0` and for each character do `total = total * b + digit_value`. `"0123456789abcdef".index(ch)` gives the digit value, and it raises ValueError for a bad character.
A mask of `count` ones is `(1 << count) - 1`. `get_bits` shifts right by `low`, then ANDs with that mask. `set_bit` uses `value | (1 << index)` to set and `value & ~(1 << index)` to clear.
`to_unsigned(n, bits)` is `n % (1 << bits)` in Python, because `%` already returns a non-negative result. `to_signed` subtracts `1 << bits` when the top bit (bit `bits - 1`) is set.
For `pack_uint`, byte number `i` counting from the least significant end is `(value >> (8 * i)) & 0xFF`. Build the list in that order, then reverse it for big-endian.
`unpack_uint` is the reverse: for little-endian, byte `i` contributes `data[i] << (8 * i)`. For big-endian, reverse the bytes first and use the same loop.
Python slices never raise for out-of-range indexes, they silently shorten. In `read_word` and `write_word`, check `0 <= addr` and `addr + size <= len(mem)` yourself and raise IndexError.
